newsitem.title: USA: USDA - 96/7 Ivory Coast cocoa crop unch, Ghana down.
newsitem.headline: USDA - 96/7 Ivory Coast cocoa crop unch, Ghana down.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Friday left its estimate for the 1996/97 Ivory Coast cocoa crop unchanged at 1.10 million tonnes but shaved its forecast for Ghana's crop by 40,000 tonnes to 350,000 tonnes.

In its Tropical Products: World Markets and Trade report, USDA also lowered its 1995/96 Ghana cocoa output forecast by 17,000 tonnes to 403,000 tonnes due to a decrease in the mid-crop production estimate.
It said total Ghana cocoa bean exports for 1995/96 and 1996/97 were reduced 17,000 tonnes and 40,000 tonnes, respectively, as a result of reduced supplies.
Last October, USDA pegged 1996/97 Ivory Coast cocoa output at 1.05 million tonnes. In March, the forecast was raised to 1.1 million tonnes based on the U.S. agricultural attache.

In Friday's report, USDA said the attache in Abidjan had revised up the main crop estimate to 950,000 tonnes from 900,000 tonnes and lowered the mid-crop estimate to 150,000 tonnes from 200,000 tonnes.

It said the main crop was revised based on actual cocoa deliveries to processors, while the mid-crop estimate was lowered due to dry weather in February that adversely affected crop flowering and development in most producing areas.
USDA said the total Ivory Coast 1996/97 export forecast for cocoa beans and products was unaffected by the change and remained at 1.21 million tonnes.
USDA said Brazil is having to import cocoa beans because of a shortfall in domestic supplies.
"According to sources, cocoa beans from Indonesia have already arrived in Brazil," USDA said in the report. "Sources estimate imports at 15,000 tons (tonnes)."
It said the cocoa beans were being imported under the drawback basis, which allows them to be imported duty free as long as there are exports of an equivalent amount of products.
